provider_policy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

provider_policy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

Which authoritative master system assigns this concept's primary identifier, and what is that identifier value?
Does the concept have a governed IRI, and which body controls the namespace it is minted in?
Which notations or classification codes denote this concept, and in which coding scheme is each one valid?
Which changes preserve the identifier, and which force a new concept identifier rather than an edit?
Which essential characteristics must an object have for it to fall under this concept?
Which delimiting characteristic separates this concept from the nearest concept it is confused with?
How is the extension bounded — open, enumerated or sampled by exemplars?
What evidence supports this delimitation — attested usage, expert ruling or a cited source clause?
When two records share designations, which test decides whether they are one concept or two?
Is this a general concept covering many objects, or an individual concept covering exactly one?
When projected into a formal ontology, is this an individual of skos:Concept, an owl:Class, or both under a documented punning rule?
Which neighbouring construct — lexical entry, word form, sense, referent, class or keyword — has previously been conflated with this record?
What distinguishes this concept record from an uncontrolled keyword or tag carrying the same string?
Which real-world objects or entity records does this concept denote, and in which model are those referents mastered?
Which exemplar, type specimen or illustration is used to show the concept without being equated with it?
Does any designation denote the referent directly rather than through the concept, and how is that recorded?
What is explicitly not a referent of this concept despite being commonly assumed to be one?
Which designation is rated preferred in each language, and which are admitted, deprecated or hidden?
What designation type is each sign — term, appellation, proper name or non-linguistic symbol?
Which rating-authority reference is carried on the designation, given that the rating process itself is governed outside this area?
Can two designations share the same rating in one language, and which constraint prevents duplicate preferred labels?
Which non-linguistic symbol represents the concept, and in what medium is that symbol fixed?
Does this designation carry its own identifier, and which system assigns it?
Which attributes are held on the designation rather than on the concept, and why does each belong there?
How is a plain-string projection kept consistent with the reified designation's single literal form?
Which relations hold between designations of the same concept, such as abbreviation of, variant of or transliteration of?
Which complete BCP 47 language tag applies to this designation, including script, region and variant subtags where they are meaningful?
Is the script subtag suppressed for this language, and if it is present anyway, what justifies including it?
Which transliteration or romanization scheme produced this designation, and what is its source designation?
Where a designation is region-specific, which territory or usage community does it apply to?
How should a consuming system behave when no designation exists for the requested language tag?
Which lexical entry realises this designation, and is it a single word, a multiword expression or an affix?
What is the canonical form of the designation, and which other forms are recorded alongside it?
Which grammatical categories are asserted, and from which data-category registry are their values drawn?
What evidence fixes the pronunciation or spoken form of this designation?
Which forms must not be treated as separate designations of the concept?
Which designations in other languages are asserted to represent this same concept, and at what degree of equivalence?
Where a target language has no designation, how is that gap recorded without coining a term?
Is equivalence asserted concept-to-concept or sense-to-sense, and what follows for downstream reuse?
What evidence supports each equivalence assertion?
Which equivalence claims are known to be partial or contested, and how is that flagged?
What is the definition text in each language, and which language tag applies to each version?
Is the definition intensional, extensional or ostensive, and which delimiting characteristic does it carry?
From which source document, clause or authority is the definition taken or adapted?
How many definitions may coexist per language, and which rule resolves competing definitions?
Which check confirms that the definition is neither circular nor a bare negation of another concept?
Which note types are recorded, and does each attach to the concept or to a specific designation?
What does the scope note state as included in and excluded from the concept's coverage?
Which examples illustrate correct and incorrect use of the designation?
Which notes are meaning-bearing and must survive interchange, and which are editorial and may be filtered?
Which subject field does this concept belong to, and from which classification is that value drawn?
Which other concept shares a designation with this one in a different subject field, and how is the pair distinguished?
Does the subject field change the concept's delimitation, or only the usage of its designations?
Which classification is authoritative for subject-field values, and what happens when it is revised?
For which audience and register is this designation appropriate — specialist, general public, regulatory or internal?
Which attested occurrence evidences that the designation is really used in this sense?
In which territory or community is the designation current, and where is it not used?
Which usage is flagged as discouraged or offensive, and which alternative is directed instead?
How is a designation's usage status kept distinct from the concept's own status?
Which concept schemes does this concept assert membership in, and is one of them designated the maintenance scheme that issues its authoritative identifier?
Does this deployment permit a concept to belong to more than one scheme, and what local rule resolves conflicting structure between those schemes?
Is membership asserted explicitly for every concept, or derived from broader, narrower or related links in this deployment?
How are concepts that assert no scheme membership treated by navigation, validation and export?
Which schemes declare this concept a top concept, and is that declaration made by the scheme rather than inferred from missing broader links?
Does a concept declared as a top concept also assert a broader concept within the same scheme, and how is that reconciled?
Which entry points should an agent use to enter a scheme's hierarchy when no top concept has been declared?
How is consistency kept when a concept is a top concept in one scheme but a mid-level concept in another?
Which collections, thesaurus arrays or concept groups include this concept, and is any of those memberships ordered?
How is the disjointness of grouping constructs from concepts enforced so that a grouping node is never resolved or exported as a concept?
Does a containing array carry a node label or facet indicator that organises siblings without itself being a retrievable concept?
Does this concept sit at a declared classification level, and what depth and ordering does that level carry?
When a grouping construct sits between a parent concept and its child concepts, is the concept-to-concept hierarchical link still asserted directly?
Which broader and narrower concepts does this concept assert, and is every one of them a direct link rather than an ancestor or descendant?
Is the transitive form of the hierarchy computed at read time, materialised in storage, or both, and how is materialised closure marked as derived?
Does this concept assert more than one broader concept, and does the governing scheme permit polyhierarchy?
How are cycles and self-referential links detected in the hierarchical graph before they enter the derived closure?
May a hierarchical link point at a concept in a different scheme, and how is such a link distinguished from a cross-scheme mapping?
What kind of hierarchical relation is asserted to each broader concept - generic, partitive, instantial or undifferentiated?
Which test must be satisfied before a hierarchical relation is asserted, and is the justification recorded with the assertion?
Which hierarchical kinds may be chained transitively in this deployment, and at which point must a chain stop?
What information is lost when a refined hierarchical kind is projected onto plain broader or narrower for interchange?
Which associative relations does this concept assert, and is a refined association subtype recorded for each?
How is the rule that an associative link must not coexist with a hierarchical path between the same two concepts checked?
Is the inverse of each associative assertion stored explicitly, inferred at read time, or both?
Which refined associative relations may be composed transitively and which are explicitly non-transitive?
Is this concept a pre-coordinated compound, and which concepts are recorded as its components?
Under which rule was this combination modelled as one concept rather than left to be combined at retrieval time?
Is the recorded decomposition lexical or semantic, and what must a consumer not infer from it?
How are the compound and its components linked without implying a hierarchical or equivalence claim between them?
Which set of target concepts jointly expresses this concept, and in which vocabulary do they sit?
Which combination operator applies to the target set, and which construct carries it when the interchange format has no compound-equivalence class?
How is a one-to-many equivalence degraded for consumers that accept only one-to-one matches, and is the loss flagged?
Is the compound equivalence reversible, and what if anything is asserted in the opposite direction?
Which mapping relation type is asserted towards each target concept, and which scheme owns that target?
What threshold distinguishes an exact match from a close match in this deployment, and who applies it?
How does the deployment handle the fact that broad and narrow matches are also hierarchical properties and therefore enter the transitive hierarchical closure?
How is the disjointness of an exact match with a broad match or a related match between the same pair of concepts enforced?
Is a mapping relation permitted between two concepts of the same scheme, and what is being asserted when it occurs?
Which mapping set or correspondence contains this concept's mapping assertions, and which two schemes does that set compare?
What cardinality does the mapping set permit, and how are many-to-many associations represented?
Which specific scheme releases does the mapping set bind to on each side?
Which mapping types may be composed across two sets to derive a third mapping, and where must composition stop?
How are contradictory mappings from different sets for the same concept pair detected and reported?
Is this a single language-independent concept carrying multilingual labels, or are language-specific concepts linked by cross-lingual mapping?
What degree of cross-lingual equivalence is recorded when the target language has no exact equivalent?
Which BCP 47 language tags, including any script and region subtags, scope each side of a cross-lingual assertion?
What must a consumer not infer from two labels carrying the same language tag or from a translated label?
Is the alignment target an ontology class, a property, an individual or another concept?
Which alignment predicate is asserted, and what entailment does it commit a consuming reasoner to?
Why is this concept not asserted as identical or class-equivalent to the ontology term by default?
How is the concept connected to lexical entries and senses without importing lexical structure into the concept record?
What closure does an export include - the concept alone, its direct relations, its whole scheme, or its transitive neighbourhood?
How are references to concepts outside the exported closure represented so they are not mistaken for missing or broken data?
Which crosswalk rule maps each local relation, grouping and mapping construct onto the target interchange model?
Which constructs are lossy on a round trip through this projection, and how is the loss declared to the consumer?
Which namespace and identifier-resolution rule applies to concept references inside the exchanged package?
Which registration states may this concept record occupy, and which are lifecycle states rather than documentation-only states?
What mandatory attributes and associations must be complete before the record may progress beyond the recorded state?
Which role must authorise each transition, and which transitions are irreversible?
What stability guarantee does each state give a downstream consumer about the concept's meaning?
Who holds decision authority over this concept, and under what documented mandate?
What proposal, review and approval steps must a change pass before publication?
What evidence, options considered and dissent must a decision capture to remain auditable?
How is a contested or appealed decision recorded without rewriting the original decision?
On what grounds may this concept be deprecated instead of corrected in place?
Which successor concept replaces the deprecated concept, and is the replacement authoritative or merely advisory?
What must a client still holding the deprecated identifier do, and until when is resolution guaranteed?
How is a retired identifier prevented from ever being reused or repointed to a different meaning?
Which immutable release of the owning concept scheme does this governed record state belong to?
How is a proposed change classified as editorial, additive or breaking, and who performs that classification?
What guarantees that a published release remains unaltered and retrievable at a later date?
How does a version designation relate to, and remain distinct from, the concept record identifier?
What atomic change was made, to which element of the concept record, and from what prior value?
Which activity, agent and prior decision caused this change?
When did the change occur, when does it take effect, and when was it ingested into this register?
How can a consumer reconstruct this concept record exactly as it stood at an arbitrary past instant?
How is an erroneous change record corrected without deleting or rewriting history?
By what evidence is another record judged to denote the same unit of thought as this one?
Which identifier survives a merge, and how are the non-surviving identifiers redirected?
When a concept is split, how are prior usages and inbound references disambiguated across the successors?
Which automated duplicate-candidate signals are used, and what false-positive tolerance is accepted before human review?
Which external source is authoritative for this concept's definition, and at what version or publication date?
Is this concept originated locally, adopted verbatim, adapted, or derived from another vocabulary?
Which agent asserted the current definition, and on whose behalf did that agent act?
How is a later change to, or withdrawal of, the authoritative source reflected in this record?
What warrant justifies admitting this as a distinct concept rather than a variant of an existing one?
Which retained attestations and citations support the current definition, and where are they held?
What counter-evidence or rejected alternative scoping was considered, and why was it set aside?
When supporting evidence cannot be published, what minimal defensible reference is exposed instead?
Which constraint sets apply to this concept record, at which severity, and who declared them applicable?
What did the most recent check return, against which record state and which constraint-set version?
Which failures block publication and which are advisory only?
What conformance to an external standard is claimed for this record, and on what evidence?
Which editorial completeness criteria has this record met, and which remain open?
How mature and stable is the definition, expressed on a governed scale?
Which quality dimension does each recorded measurement address, and by which metric was it computed?
Who last reviewed the editorial content, and when is the next review due?
Which organisation owns this concept record, and which named steward maintains it?
What is the escalation and hand-over path when the steward is unavailable or the role lapses?
Which responsibilities are delegated to a contributor without transferring ownership?
How is a change of owning organisation recorded without breaking identifier continuity?
Which namespace mints this concept's identifier, and which body controls that namespace?
What resolution and persistence commitment is made for the identifier, and for how long?
How are identifiers minted, reserved and prevented from collision or reuse across the namespace?
What happens to identifiers if the namespace is transferred, forked or discontinued?
Under which licence may this concept record and its attached evidence be reused?
Which parts of the record are restricted, to which parties, and on what stated basis?
Is any content embargoed, and which event or instant releases the embargo?
Does any attached evidence identify a living person or carry third-party rights that constrain publication?
Which retention class applies to this record and to each attached evidence item?
Which authority approves and executes disposition, and what evidence of execution is returned?
Is the record under a hold that suspends disposition, and what releases that hold?
What minimum tombstone must survive after disposition so that references do not silently break?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
